societies.name: Mindjammer — Commonality Core Worlds

scope.period: Second Age of Space, established Core provision before any particular adventure crisis
scope.population: Living human and active human-derived Core residents
exclusions: Every constituent locality as institutionally identical
Dormant files and temporary avatar copies as extra people

societies.description:
In the Commonality’s Core Worlds, makepoints turn energy into food and ordinary materials, making day-to-day necessities readily obtainable without ordinary subsistence wages. The author explicitly distinguishes this abundance from the Fringe, where technology may be absent or embargoed. The guarantee estimate is therefore strong for the functioning Core rather than for every world claimed by the Commonality. Rare goods and supply chains can still constrain particular desires.

The gathered passages do not establish who can effectively overrule resource allocation across these diverse worlds. Control remains unresolved instead of equating an advanced socialist description with equal ownership or mistaking a Mindscape network for a sovereign AI. Citizens can still undertake exploration, research, administration and care, so freedom from scarcity does not imply that everyone stops useful work. The record verifies the tabletop setting; a novel in the same universe is not automatically evidence for this precise economic scope.

guarantees.basis: Author answers establish actual makepoint air/food/material synthesis; the Core sourcebook passage explicitly makes ordinary necessities trivial to obtain.

control.basis: The bounded author and Core passages leave effective ownership/override institutions unresolved.

nonworking.basis: No all-person useful-work census; voluntary research, care, art and administration still count.

evidence.claim: Author answers establish actual makepoint air/food/material synthesis; the Core sourcebook passage explicitly makes ordinary necessities trivial to obtain.
evidence.locator: Named polity and bounded economic/provision sections

uncertainties: Reference-led provisional assessment; local variation remains.
The bounded author and Core passages leave effective ownership/override institutions unresolved.
Chosen useful activities count as work; no employment statistic is silently converted to nonworking.

societies.name: Orion’s Arm — Terragen Federation

scope.population: Living humans and active human-derived residents within established Federation provision
exclusions: Every constituent locality as institutionally identical
Dormant files and temporary avatar copies as extra people

societies.description:
The Terragen Federation places largely human cultures within the mature Sephirotic productive system. The setting’s shared baseline is easy access to food, shelter and other necessities, with houses, commerce and prestige still important above that floor. This supports a provisional strong guarantee assessment within established settlements. It does not turn every backworld or every social group into an identical utopia, and the federation’s prejudices and powerful Houses remain relevant qualifications.

Yave’s administrative interventions coexist with local institutions and inherited economic power. The ruler’s origin in an ascended Federation representative also makes a simple external-AI label unsafe. Effective human control is left unresolved, with concentrated institutions and higher-mind supervision both visible. Human and active human-derived residents form the explicit population scope rather than a total of all artificial beings. Research, administration, commerce and cultural production continue; neither Federation ideals nor an automatic material floor supplies an all-person nonworking percentage.

societies.name: Orion’s Arm — Cyberian uploaded residents
societies.society: Active human-derived residents of maintained Cyberian virches

scope.period: Current-era functioning Mirror Court hosted environments
scope.population: Active human-derived uploads in Cyberian environments, a minority of the broader AI/alife population
exclusions: Every constituent locality as institutionally identical
Dormant files and temporary avatar copies as extra people

societies.description:
Cyberian virtual worlds are implemented, continuing environments supported by physical computronium and a hierarchy that maintains infrastructure and cyber-immunity. Active human-derived uploads form a minority of this much larger artificial population. Their ongoing access to a viable environment, rather than disembodiment alone, is the qualifying provision mechanism. Guarantees receive a cautious favorable estimate because the infrastructure is maintained, while administrator restrictions and differing local virtual societies limit any claim of unconditional rights.

The Mirror Court regulates environments and acceptable behavior, with higher-level entities administering lower ones. The exact origins of those administrators and residents’ effective resource powers are not fully resolved here, so control stays null rather than classifying every posthuman higher mind as an external AI. Processing allocations and substrate leases remain real resource issues. Digital design, research, administration and artistic creation are useful work, and billions of voluntary social groups do not provide a nonworking census. Dormant backups and temporary forks are not added as separate leisure citizens.

guarantees.basis: Mirror Court administration explicitly maintains infrastructure and cyber-immunity for continuing active virtual residents.

control.basis: Hierarchical higher-mind administration is clear, but its origins and residents’ ultimate resource powers remain insufficiently resolved.

nonworking.basis: No all-person useful-work census; voluntary research, care, art and administration still count.

societies.name: Orion’s Arm — NoCoZo

scope.population: Living human and active human-derived denizens of established NoCoZo settlements
exclusions: Every constituent locality as institutionally identical
Dormant files and temporary avatar copies as extra people

societies.description:
NoCoZo retains pervasive markets on top of post-scarcity production. Food, shelter and bandwidth are readily available because firms that deny basics face reputation penalties. Small charges or conditions may remain, including a share of future income or access to dreams for advertising research. Guarantees are therefore favorable but qualified: widespread practical access is stronger than a harsh survival market, while reputation enforcement differs from an unconditional public entitlement.

Private property, competing institutions and powerful higher minds coexist. The Invisible Hand can reshape markets through financial intervention even though the Zone has no single formal ruler. Neither statelessness nor plentiful individual firms proves equal human control of the productive system, so the control coordinate remains unresolved. Frequent transactions are also not a work census: collecting an income or consuming a service is not necessarily useful labor. The record is scoped to human and active human-derived denizens and does not count all artificial market agents as humans.

guarantees.basis: The reference explicitly combines post-scarcity infrastructure with easy basic food/shelter/bandwidth and possible limited charges.

control.basis: Private ownership, polycentric institutions and hidden higher-mind market intervention prevent a simple distributed-human or autonomous-AI coordinate.

societies.name: Orion’s Arm — Metasoft’s Wurm baseline reserve
societies.society: Deliberately primitive human preservation under advanced vec guardians

scope.period: The maintained Palaeolithic reserve described in current-era Metasoft reference lore
scope.population: Living baseline humans in the Wurm reserve

societies.description:
Wurm preserves baseline humans in a Palaeolithic hunter-gatherer setting while the surrounding Metasoft civilization possesses self-replicating industry and sophisticated machine infrastructure. Human subsistence activity remains real even though the guardians could permit a far more automated way of life. This is an interpretive zero variant based on deliberate technological restriction for preservation, rather than a claim that Metasoft wants to protect employment. It does not describe the relaxed or fully integrated reserves.

Ultimate control over the permitted technological setting belongs to the vec guardians, near the autonomous-machine end of the map. Guardianship of the reserve does not establish an individual guarantee of food, shelter or care inside its primitive ecology, so the material-guarantee coordinate remains unresolved. Hunting, gathering and other useful activities count as work; the end of human employment in the original Metasoft corporation is not a census for this later human population. The point concerns living humans under a maintained restriction regime, not the labor participation of robot citizens.

guarantees.basis: Reserve protection and deliberate primitive technology are verified, but an individual material floor inside Wurm is not.

control.basis: Independent Metasoft vec guardians determine the permissible technology of the human reserve.

nonworking.basis: No all-person useful-work census; voluntary research, care, art and administration still count.

evidence.locator: Named polity and bounded economic/provision sections

societies.name: Orion’s Arm — Zoeific Flow society
societies.society: Engineered ecological provision and voluntary adaptive roles

scope.population: Living human-derived Zoeific residents within the Flow, an explicit posthuman comparison
exclusions: Every constituent locality as institutionally identical
Dormant files and temporary avatar copies as extra people

societies.description:
The Flow links engineered organisms, infrastructure and residents into a needs-responsive productive ecology. Consumption prompts new resource-producing biota, while entertainment and life-support requirements are communicated through the same system. Provision therefore does not require ordinary wages for each necessity. The favorable guarantee estimate is qualified by local conditions and the Flow’s powerful influence over bodies and preferences. Refusing a proposed role is allowed, and another participant or a grown organism can replace the refuser.

The ruling higher minds distribute the behavioral rules, while residents actively maintain their institutions and often accept several useful roles. Their biological and posthuman nature prevents a simple external-machine control classification, so control remains unresolved. A low, broad nonworking estimate follows the explicit high economic participation and widespread roles; this is an editorial direction, not a canonical percentage. Enjoyable work still counts, including waste processing, ecological care and traffic coordination. The human-derived population is an explicit comparison within a much broader ecology of recognized persons.

guarantees.basis: Engineered needs-responsive biota provide resources, and a refused role can be filled by another candidate or a grown organism.

control.basis: Higher minds set Flow rules, but biological/posthuman ruler origins and ordinary effective control are not reduced to machine sovereignty.

nonworking.basis: Most citizens take multiple useful roles and participation is explicitly high; .1 [0,.4] is a broad noncanonical direction, not an all-person census.

societies.name: Orion’s Arm — Negentropic household provision
societies.society: AI-governed citizens supplied through Genius Loci

scope.population: Living humans and active human-derived citizens receiving the described household provision
exclusions: Every constituent locality as institutionally identical
Dormant files and temporary avatar copies as extra people

societies.description:
Negentropic household fabricators supply food, consumables, security and home management. The reference explicitly says citizens’ basic needs are met, while frivolous or wasteful requests can be refused. This supports strong guarantees without pretending that every luxury is available on demand. Resource discipline and moral supervision are meaningful constraints, but they are not automatically evidence that ordinary residents must earn subsistence through wages.

The Alliance’s AI cluster and its Precepts set the governing limits, placing effective control near the autonomous-AI end rather than distributed human ownership. Local cultures remain diverse within those limits. Citizens can try to persuade household systems to allow luxuries and can still conduct science, culture and other useful activity. None of this provides a complete work census, so nonworking remains unresolved. The scope is the described functioning household system for human and active human-derived citizens, not an assertion that every frontier site or every historical Negentropic settlement offers identical services.

societies.name: Orion’s Arm — Solar Dominion
societies.society: Lord of Rays governed Sephirotic provision

scope.period: Current-era established Dominion before any particular local emergency
scope.population: Living human and active human-derived residents of established Dominion settlements
exclusions: Every constituent locality as institutionally identical
Dormant files and temporary avatar copies as extra people

societies.description:
The Solar Dominion combines the Sephirotic baseline of readily available necessities with direct higher-machine government. The shared economic reference establishes easy access to basic food, shelter and bandwidth; the Dominion reference establishes who governs this particular population. Guarantees are provisionally favorable for established settlements, while local conditions and the demands of the religious-political order remain qualifications. Submission to that order is not by itself evidence that ordinary food is purchased only through wages.

The Lord of Rays rules through the God-Emperor interface, prefects, priests and sympathetic AI systems. The reference explicitly describes this as AI rule, placing control close to the autonomous-machine end despite the presence of human intermediaries. This does not erase meaningful local institutions or the different experiences of frontier populations. Useful research, culture, care and administration continue, so a provisioned population is not assumed to be wholly nonworking. Human and active human-derived residents are the disclosed denominator rather than every simulated or artificial agent.
